title: Six killed in shooting at Krakow's main square, Polish media report
dek: A gunman fired from a car in the centre of one of Poland's best known cities. Motive is not known, and posts are already giving it different names.
what: On the afternoon of Saturday 7 November, a gunman fired from a car near Krakow's Main Market Square. The BBC first reported that Polish police said five people were killed and around a dozen injured. CTV News gave 12 injured. JPost reported that the suspect wore military-style clothing and used a long firearm, and that police shot him and detained him.

Later reporting raises the toll. The Polish daily Rzeczpospolita reports six dead and 15 wounded, including police officers, and says the suspect is a 24-year-old Polish citizen who held a firearms permit and was not known to police. It quotes officials saying he was not a soldier and had never served. It quotes Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski saying shots were fired within three minutes of the call, which prevented a much larger massacre. I read the Rzeczpospolita report through a summary, not in full, and these figures have not been checked against a police statement.

I could not find an official statement on motive. Some posts call it a terror attack. One post says it happened near a protest against the EU and Tusk and blames Brussels. None of the reports I opened mentions a protest, and I could not confirm one. Posts also describe other bodies found elsewhere; I could not confirm that. This story does not name the suspect.
why: A mass shooting in a historic city centre, where public shootings are rare, drew fast posting from news accounts before the facts were in. Early posts filled the gap on motive.
next: Statements from Polish police or prosecutors on motive, and the final count of dead and injured.

corrections.text: The toll was raised from five dead and about a dozen injured to six dead and 15 wounded, per Rzeczpospolita.
